# Line charts and bar charts

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

print("=== Line Charts ===\n")

# Sample data
dates = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun']
player_count = [150, 180, 220, 280, 350, 420]
active_players = [120, 150, 190, 240, 300, 360]

# Line chart
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(dates, player_count, 'b-o', linewidth=2, markersize=8, label='Total Players')
plt.plot(dates, active_players, 'r-s', linewidth=2, markersize=8, label='Active Players')

plt.title('Player Growth Over Time')
plt.xlabel('Month')
plt.ylabel('Number of Players')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

plt.show()

print("Line chart displayed!")

print("\n=== Multiple Lines ===\n")

# More data
months = np.arange(1, 13)
daily = np.random.randint(30, 60, 12)
weekly = np.random.randint(50, 80, 12)

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

# Different line styles
plt.plot(months, daily, 'g--', label='Daily Players')
plt.plot(months, weekly, 'b-', label='Weekly Players')

# Fill between
plt.fill_between(months, daily, weekly, alpha=0.3)

plt.title('Player Activity by Period')
plt.xlabel('Month')
plt.ylabel('Players')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.show()

print("\n=== Bar Charts ===\n")

# Bar chart
classes = ['Warrior', 'Mage', 'Rogue', 'Archer', 'Paladin']
counts = [45, 38, 42, 35, 40]

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

# Vertical bar chart
plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
plt.bar(classes, counts, color=['blue', 'green', 'red', 'purple', 'orange'])
plt.title('Class Distribution (Vertical)')
plt.xlabel('Class')
plt.ylabel('Count')

# Horizontal bar chart
plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
plt.barh(classes, counts, color=['blue', 'green', 'red', 'purple', 'orange'])
plt.title('Class Distribution (Horizontal)')
plt.xlabel('Count')
plt.ylabel('Class')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print("\n=== Grouped Bar Chart ===\n")

# Grouped data
classes = ['Warrior', 'Mage', 'Rogue']
levels = ['Level 1-10', 'Level 11-20', 'Level 21+']

# Data: [class, levels]
data = {
    'Warrior': [15, 20, 10],
    'Mage': [12, 18, 8],
    'Rogue': [10, 22, 10]
}

x = np.arange(len(levels))
width = 0.25

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

for i, (class_name, values) in enumerate(data.items()):
    plt.bar(x + i*width, values, width, label=class_name)

plt.xlabel('Level Range')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.title('Class Distribution by Level Range')
plt.xticks(x + width, levels)
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

plt.show()

phase1.explanation:
🐍 **Line and bar charts are the most common visualizations.**

**Line charts:**
```python
# Basic line
plt.plot(x, y)

# With markers
plt.plot(x, y, 'o-', markersize=5)

# Multiple lines
plt.plot(x, y1, label='Line 1')
plt.plot(x, y2, label='Line 2')

# Fill between
plt.fill_between(x, y1, y2, alpha=0.3)
```

**Bar charts:**
```python
# Vertical
plt.bar(x, y)

# Horizontal
plt.barh(x, y)

# Grouped
width = 0.25
plt.bar(x - width, values1, width, label='Group1')
plt.bar(x, values2, width, label='Group2')
plt.bar(x + width, values3, width, label='Group3')

# Stacked
plt.bar(x, values1, label='Group1')
plt.bar(x, values2, bottom=values1, label='Group2')
```

**Line styles:**
- `'-'` solid
- `'--'` dashed
- `'-.'` dash-dot
- `':'` dotted

**Marker styles:**
- `'o'` circle
- `'s'` square
- `'^'` triangle
- `'*'` star

phase2.explanation:
**Too many categories makes bar charts unreadable!**

**What's wrong:**
1. 50 categories with 50 bars
2. Labels overlap or are too small
3. Pattern is hard to see

**The fix:**
```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# Method 1: Show only top N
values = np.random.randint(1, 100, 50)
indices = np.argsort(values)[-10:]  # Top 10
categories = [f'Cat_{i}' for i in indices]
top_values = values[indices]

plt.bar(categories, top_values)
plt.title('Top 10 Categories')
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.show()

# Method 2: Use horizontal bars
plt.barh(categories, values[:15])  # First 15
plt.title('Horizontal Bars (more readable)')
plt.show()

# Method 3: Use a different plot type
# - Box plot
# - Scatter plot
# - Histogram
```
